synthesis.headline: Stop adding context to the implementer prompt — every proposal that lands more structured text at the implementer is the same shape as semantic_bridge/translation_facts. Build the three structural-change spikes first: inner cslc loop (#1), layout-contract gate-and-repair (#2), runtime-trace augmentation for halo hangs (#3). Total spike cost ~26 engineering hours; together they falsify or validate seven other proposals.

top_3.name: Compile-and-edit inner loop (cslc-in-the-loop drafter) — minimal-spike variant
top_3.why_top: Both critiques rated unlikely at full scope, BUT both proposed essentially the same 4-hour falsification: bypass reviewer/architect on cslc-failure, re-prompt same implementer session with just the top-N cslc error lines, up to k micro-iterations. This is the cheapest test of the load-bearing claim that the current 8-attempt outer loop wastes most of its budget on context perturbation rather than focused syntax repair. Critically distinct from translation_facts because the signal is execution-derived AND injected post-draft, not pre-draft — and unlike halo-gotcha r4, the harness IS the real bundle, not a minimal synthetic. The 4-hour version doubles as the gate for several other proposals (sectioned synthesis, sub-kernel probe gate, syntax-fixer model) so a null result here kills three branches at once. Best cost-information ratio in the entire brainstorm.
top_3.first_concrete_step: Edit /home/USER/xkernel/code_translation/cuda2csl.py around line 1469 (post-extract_code_block, pre-_benchmark_current_code). Add a pre-benchmark cslc dry-run via the bundle's commands_wse3.sh head section, or reuse ground_gotcha._run_cslc against the real bundle dir. On rc!=0: extract first 3 file:line:error lines, re-prompt the SAME implementer session with just those lines + 'patch only the named lines, return full file', cap at k=3 micro-iterations, then proceed to normal benchmark. Add XKERNEL_INNER_CSLC_LOOP=1 env flag for A/B. Run on the 9 failing W1 kernels, 1 attempt each (compare against attempt 1 of last hybrid sweep).
top_3.gate: ≥2 NEW passes on the 9-kernel failure corpus that current attempt-1 does not produce, with 0 regressions on the 6 currently-passing kernels. If 0-1 new passes: kill the entire inner-loop direction. If ≥3: scale to full 8-attempt + cluster gating.

top_3.name: Layout-extracted contract enforcement pre-cslc — as a deterministic lint+repair gate (NOT pre-prompt facts injection)
top_3.why_top: Real structural difference from translation_facts: extraction code already exists (translation_facts.py _extract_export_names/_extract_imports/_extract_declared_task_ids), but this proposal USES the extracted facts as a mechanical REJECT-AND-REPAIR gate post-generation rather than as pre-prompt context. The discriminator vs translation_facts is binary: does the linter actually fire on >20% of attempts AND catch the stub-pe.csl / file-not-found / queue-0-collision failure modes the latest sweep shows are real? Two critiques converged on the same gating diagnostic: run extractor + diff against existing failed attempts in results/ first, count fire-rate. The audit IS the experiment. Targets dsr_queue_fabric_init (named failure cluster) and the stub-output failure mode (~5 of 72 failed attempts in latest sweep, per critic data). Cheap, deterministic, reuses shipped code.
top_3.first_concrete_step: Half-day audit FIRST: write a 50-line script that walks results/hybrid_sweep_20260614_210137/**/*.csl, runs translation_facts._extract_* against each failed pe.csl + the kernel's layout.csl, and counts (a) name/contract violations, (b) stub outputs (<500 chars, no comptime block), (c) queue-0-or-1 usage, (d) memcpy-reserved task ID usage. Tabulate per cluster. THEN if fire rate is >20% on failing-9, wire into cuda2csl.py as a synthetic 'bucket=L' (lint failure) that short-circuits cslc with a structured diff prompt — same path as bucket-C repair.
top_3.gate: Audit gate: linter fires on ≥20% of failed attempts in the existing failure corpus, with <5% false-positive rate against the 28 known-passing pe.csl files. Sweep gate: ≥1 NEW pass on the 9-kernel failure corpus AND wall-time-per-failed-attempt drops ≥15s on average (catching errors locally vs cslc). If FP >5% on known-passing OR fire-rate <10% on failing: kill — the bottleneck isn't symbol allocation.

top_3.name: csdb / sdk_debug_shell wavelet replay as runtime-failure diagnosis — hand-curated 3-kernel pilot
top_3.why_top: Only proposal that addresses the halo runtime-hang failure mode (the dominant cluster, 6/7) at the layer where the failure actually manifests: device state, not source text. All other halo-targeted proposals (skeleton-IR, exemplar retrieval, SMT linter, sub-kernel probe) attack the WRITING side; this attacks the READING side at runtime. Critiques disagree on whether the implementer can act on the signal even when given it — so the pilot IS that test. Critic verified the tools exist (sdk_debug_shell with --x/--y/--color/--backpressure flags, csdb in /home/USER/cs_sdk-1.4.0/bin). Failure-time grounding, narrow conditional firing (only on hangs), reuses debugger_agent sub-agent infrastructure already in place. If pilot is 0/3, eliminates an entire class of proposed interventions (the runtime-trace branch).
top_3.first_concrete_step: Phase 0 gating pilot, 1 day, no production code. Pick 3 currently-failing halo_recv_unblock kernels with confirmed runtime hangs (not compile fails). For each, manually run sdk_debug_shell wavelet-trace and instr-trace tasks across the rectangle, hand-format the per-PE blocked-state output to ~2KB, paste into the existing debugger_agent's DebuggerInput.stderr_tail slot as augmentation. Re-run the same (model, seed, temp) configuration and observe whether the next implementer attempt produces a different recommended_patch that compiles AND advances.
top_3.gate: ≥1 of 3 pilot halo kernels flips to passing with hand-curated trace augmentation. If 0/3: kill the entire runtime-trace direction (LLM can't convert PE-stuck-on-color-N into a structural fix). If 2-3/3: invest in the parser (4-6 days) and the per-PE scan logic that sdk_debug_shell requires (it takes --x/--y inputs, doesn't return 'which PE is stuck' — that loop must be built).

ranked_runners_up.name: Iterative-solver run.py rewrite (host-loop → on-device loop)
ranked_runners_up.short_reason: Not in the original 35 proposals as a standalone, but surfaced by multiple critiques as the actual unlock for 4 of the 9 W1-failing iterative solvers (BiCGSTAB, CG, PCG, Power_Method). The auto-memory note explicitly identifies the root cause (cycles_send measures host↔device RPC sync, not on-device compute) and a 0-attempt-needed mitigation. The 'W1 failing 9/15' headline is misleading: the true addressable W1 residual is ~5 kernels, not 9. Highest-leverage non-pipeline item in the entire survey; do this before any further W1 or W2 investment on the immune-kernels family.

ranked_runners_up.name: Nearest-neighbor skeleton seeding from passing kernels — hand-crafted single-kernel spike
ranked_runners_up.short_reason: Both critiques converged on the same kill-gate: hand-author ONE skeleton from Laplacian2D-Halo/pe.csl for the closest-matched failing halo kernel, run 5 attempts. 0/5 = dead. 2+/5 = real signal worth the index+abstractor build. ~4 hours. Genuinely structurally distinct from translation_facts (constraint surface, not prose), but the leak-vs-utility tradeoff (if it teaches structure, it leaks structure) is unresolved. Worth running AFTER the inner-loop spike.

ranked_runners_up.name: Profile-guided KB miner — 1-hour histogram FIRST, build the pipeline only if data warrants
ranked_runners_up.short_reason: Zero LLM cost to extract the histogram from existing logs (one bash one-liner per critic). If the histogram shows 3+ actionable non-cascade non-already-covered patterns, the full pipeline is worth 3-4 days. If it shows mostly 'semantic error in module imported here' cascade noise + 'compile-fine-but-hang' for halo (predicted), it's dead. The histogram itself feeds the next round of hand-curated grounded gotchas regardless — net positive even on a kill verdict.

ranked_runners_up.name: Single dsr_queue boilerplate injector (5-line deterministic post-edit)
ranked_runners_up.short_reason: Cheapest member of the template-library family. Hand-write the @initialize_queue + @is_arch wse3 boilerplate insertion as a 30-line Python post-edit pass triggered when @get_input_queue with non-default color is detected and the wrapping @initialize_queue is missing. Run cslc; if compiles, accept. If +1-2 W1 wins, generalizes to full template-library proposal. If 0, kills templating direction at 1/40 the cost of the full 15-template build.

ranked_runners_up.name: Drop-the-hard-kernels strategic exit — but with the corrected kernel list
ranked_runners_up.short_reason: The reallocation idea is structurally sound and not isomorphic to any discarded experiment, but the original 9-kernel hit list is wrong (4 are W2-stuck due to host-RPC measurement bug, not W1-stuck). The correct version: (a) fix run.py for iterative solvers per runner-up #1, (b) graduate kernels only after one fresh sweep with the 3 new halo gotchas live measures the actual ceiling. Bundle with the run.py rewrite above.

rejected_with_reason.name: Reference-CSL retrieval via structural similarity over ground-truth pe.csl corpus
rejected_with_reason.reason: W1 invariant violation — the corpus IS the answer key for 5+ of 15 benchmark kernels (verified via diff: xkernel/kernels/GEMV Collectives 2D/CSL/pe.csl equals csl-examples/benchmarks/gemv-collectives_2d/pe.csl byte-for-byte). Either anonymization is weak (leak) or strong (collapses to prose-RAG = translation_facts shape, 0W/2L/17T). Author's own kill-gate would by my reading return kill on most halo patterns since the 3 shipped grounded gotchas already encode the skeleton.

rejected_with_reason.name: Retrieval over our own version_trace.json (success ICL)
rejected_with_reason.reason: Success index is ~5-6 distinct kernels, mostly iterative solvers that 'pass' due to a known measurement bug (host-RPC-bound cycles_send) — not translation-quality successes. Cluster mismatch fatal: failing clusters {halo, dsr, c2d} have ~zero structural neighbors in the success set. Same shape as semantic_bridge + contamination risk on near-duplicate variant kernels.

rejected_with_reason.name: Two-stage retrieval: cluster-classifier → dense-embedding rerank
rejected_with_reason.reason: Closest in shape to translation_facts of any proposal — same prompt slot, same corpus, just better-ranked chunks. r2/r3/r4 halo evidence: bottleneck is composition not retrieval (canonical hints injected directly still scored 0/5). Author's own audit-first kill criterion (rank-overlap >70% = abandon) likely to trigger immediately on the small uniform corpus.

rejected_with_reason.name: AST-diff guided patch retrieval (post-compile-success, pre-numeric-fail)
rejected_with_reason.reason: Bucket D does not exist. Critics audited 114 verdicted attempts in the latest resweep: A=4, B=102, C=8, D=0. 'numeric-mismatch-with-compile-success' is empirically near-zero of the failure mass; the 9 failing kernels die at compile or at runtime hang, not at wrong-numerical-output. Phantom-bucket targeting.

rejected_with_reason.name: Specialist syntax-fixer model (small/fast) gated by cslc
rejected_with_reason.reason: Critic empirically extracted last-attempt cslc stderr from 9 failing W1 kernels and found 0/9 are clean line-local syntax-typo errors a Haiku fixer could correctly resolve without seeing layout.csl + commands.sh + the export contract. Most errors are cross-file contract failures. Killed by data.

rejected_with_reason.name: Self-critique against cslc-grounded checklist
rejected_with_reason.reason: Critic grep'd terminal errors and found 0 of 9 W1 failures are checklist-class violations. Failures are 'tensor_access uses runtime pointer', 'layout_mod.get_x_coord at module scope', '@export_symbol type mismatch', 'param sizing chain broken' — none fit the 4-item YES/NO format. Same shape as translation_facts at a downstream slot.

rejected_with_reason.name: Reverse translation (csl2cuda) as automatic differentiator
rejected_with_reason.reason: csl2cuda.py is itself an LLM agent, not a deterministic extractor. The 'execution-grounded' claim is false: the diff would be between two LLM beliefs about the algorithm. csl2cuda's own success matrix is 13/21, with the 8 failures overlapping W1 failures — guaranteeing garbage reverse-pass on the targets. Same shape as semantic_bridge.

rejected_with_reason.name: Sub-kernel cslc probe gate before bundle assembly
rejected_with_reason.reason: Actual cslc errors are dominated by cross-file constructs (`semantic error in module imported here`, `name not declared during layout evaluation`, `param uninitialized`). These are by definition NOT fragment-isolable. Same composition wall that killed halo-gotcha r4.

rejected_with_reason.name: Static halo-recv counting linter (compile-time invariant check)
rejected_with_reason.reason: Canonical halo patterns are heterogeneous: Game-of-Life uses @block(microthread_handle) per-edge join (no counter); Laplacian2D-Halo uses RX_DONE_TID; benchmark-libs uses param-driven imports. The 'recv_count == threshold' model matches NONE of them. Encoding mismatch = highest-risk failure mode.

rejected_with_reason.name: Symbolic SMT check of recv/unblock parity from layout
rejected_with_reason.reason: Same encoding-mismatch problem as the static linter, plus 7-10 day Z3 modeling cost. Will false-positive on multi-channel state machines. No prior art for SMT-on-LLM-emitted-DSL.

rejected_with_reason.name: Iterative deepening: 1-PE prototype, then scale
rejected_with_reason.reason: Compute layer is NOT the failing layer. Single-Tile-Matvec (compute-only) already passes; failures are at fabric/halo/dsr — the very layer this proposal strips out for phase 1. Scale-up phase still has to invent halo wiring from scratch (halo-r4 already failed at this, 0/5).

rejected_with_reason.name: Plan-then-verify: architect emits a checkable structural spec before implementation
rejected_with_reason.reason: Highest acknowledged collision risk with translation_facts. The validator's checkable surface (imports, exports, task_id_vars, fabric_colors) is exactly what translation_facts extracted. Halo failures live in handler-body semantics the schema cannot express. Architect's prose plans are already approximately correct on the surface.

rejected_with_reason.name: Self-consistency vote with kernel-level execution oracle
rejected_with_reason.reason: Sonnet+Opus union at 6/15 with model diversity already represents the BoN regime. Same-model T=1.0 sampling on halo failures will mode-collapse to identical wrong skeletons. singularity_gate serializes cslc, breaking the parallelism claim. Consensus-signature feedback collapses to translation_facts shape.

rejected_with_reason.name: Executable mini-IR: Python reference runner that validates translation semantics pre-cslc
rejected_with_reason.reason: Wrong failure-mode model. Failures are CSL-protocol bugs (queue collisions, missing unblock, fabric init order) not algorithm-decomposition bugs. Architect designs for halo kernels are usually algorithmically correct; bugs live below the IR's abstraction level. 12-op list would balloon to MLIR-scale.

rejected_with_reason.name: CUDA-side AST IR: tree-sitter parse + structural feature vector
rejected_with_reason.reason: Both decisions the IR would drive (cluster detection, retrieval) are already being made correctly per critic audits. Bottleneck is composition not retrieval. AST adds a signal where signal isn't missing.

rejected_with_reason.name: CUDA-vs-CSL property-based equivalence sweep with K=8 randomized inputs
rejected_with_reason.reason: Cannot run on the failing cluster: halo/dsr/collectives_2d kernels bake fabric_dims and PE grid into the CSL bundle at cslc time. Only gates kernels that already pass — addresses the floor, not the ceiling. W1 lift = 0 by construction.

rejected_with_reason.name: Per-section CSL synthesis with cslc gate on each section
rejected_with_reason.reason: Non-local cross-section dependencies make per-section validation degrade to whole-file compilation by section 4 (admitted in 'cumulative compilation' mitigation). halo failures are mostly cslc-clean runtime hangs — per-section cslc cannot catch them. The inner-cslc-loop variant in top-3 captures the same benefit at 1/10 cost.

rejected_with_reason.name: Skeleton-IR full version (auto-emitter from layout.csl + 6-template catalog)
rejected_with_reason.reason: Halo cluster is heterogeneous (Laplacian, Reduce, LorenzoPredictor, Residual, 25-pt-Stencil all have structurally different file decompositions). 6-template catalog is realistically 15-20 templates. Hand-crafted spike variant (runner-up) is the right test of principle without the auto-emitter cost.

rejected_with_reason.name: Compile-validated few-shot construction (full 8-15 card bank)
rejected_with_reason.reason: Halo-gotcha r4 already established that minimal-harness canonical patterns are 'too composed to fit'. Cards must either contain enough composition to teach (fail leak-gate) or abstract enough to pass leak-gate (then prose-equivalent gotchas). One-card pilot on dsr_queue (kept in runner-ups) is the right falsifier.

rejected_with_reason.name: Differential debugger: compile-error → grounded-snippet retrieval
rejected_with_reason.reason: Existing debugger_agent.py + bucket-B repair already does failure-conditioned grounded-snippet injection. ab_debugger_20260601 A/B was 1/4 vs 1/4 — null result on the same architecture. Lookup-table instead of LLM-generated patch is strictly less expressive.

rejected_with_reason.name: Test-time scaling: 32-candidate parallel sampling with cslc-gated voting
rejected_with_reason.reason: Sonnet+Opus union ceiling (6/15) measured at 8 sequential attempts per model with bucket-routed repair — sequential conditioning on cslc errors is richer than T=0.9 jitter. Verifier swap to DESIGN.md cosine is strictly worse than current cycle-based ranker. singularity_gate serializes cslc.

rejected_with_reason.name: Bench corpus split: pseudo refs (numpy-mesh-explicit) for the failing kernels
rejected_with_reason.reason: Writing the pseudo IS doing the architect's job. 2-eng-week cost for diagnostic information already available from mode_cuda_nl. dsr_queue / collectives_2d failures are protocol-realization bugs, not algorithm-shape bugs.

rejected_with_reason.name: Co-design feedback loop: file SDK issues + local cslc wrapper
rejected_with_reason.reason: Upstream-issues half: not a framework improvement, multi-quarter latency. Local wrapper half: reduces to 'inject reworded gotcha into debugger stderr_tail' — same shape as cluster-keyed gotcha injection that already exists. halo-r4 evidence: even cslc-grounded canonical patterns + injected = 0/5.

synthesis.meta_observation: The 35-proposal × 70-critique survey produces a sharp negative finding: every proposal that lands MORE STRUCTURED CONTEXT in the implementer prompt (whether before generation, after generation as critique, after generation as retrieved exemplar, or extracted from CUDA / extracted from layout / extracted from past successes) lands in the same dead-zone as semantic_bridge and translation_facts. This is now four distinct shapes of 'better input to the same implementer call' that have failed or are predicted to fail (semantic_bridge: prose mapping; translation_facts: YAML facts; halo-r2/r3/r4: canonical patterns; and 7+ proposals here). Meanwhile, every proposal that critics rated as 'worth a spike' — the inner cslc loop, the layout-contract gate-and-repair, the runtime-trace augmentation, the hand-crafted skeleton-seed, the dsr_queue boilerplate post-edit — changes the PIPELINE STRUCTURE, not the prompt. The bottleneck is NOT 'the implementer needs to know more'; the implementer already gets layout.csl + cluster gotchas + cslc stderr + reviewer rationale + debugger report + builtin whitelist verbatim. The bottleneck is 'the implementer cannot COMPOSE multi-construct CSL idioms in a single shot regardless of context quality.' That diagnosis points at three directions, in priority order: (1) execution-in-the-loop at finer granularity than 'whole-file → whole-benchmark' (the inner cslc loop), (2) constraint enforcement by code rather than by prompt (the layout-contract gate), (3) failure-time observability at the layer where failures actually manifest (runtime traces for halo hangs). Crucially, a separate finding: 4 of the 9 'W1-failing' iterative solvers (Power_Method, BiCGSTAB, CG, PCG) are NOT capability-limited — they're blocked by a known measurement bug per project_power_method_instrumentation.md (host-RPC-bound cycles_send + dead-code editing). The true addressable W1 residual is ~5 kernels, not 9, and the run.py rewrite should be elevated above any new translation-pipeline work for that family. Final note: the survey reveals a process gap — most proposals named multi-day engineering investments but had 4-hour falsification spikes that would have killed them cheaply. The framework's discipline going forward should be 'no proposal ships without the spike first', and the brainstorm itself should be filtered through that gate before scoring.

all_proposals.name: Skeleton-IR: typed pe.csl scaffold with TODO blocks the LLM fills
all_proposals.one_line: Stop free-text generation of the whole pe.csl; emit a typed skeleton (params, imports, queue reservations, task IDs, comptime blocks, fn signatures) deterministically from layout.csl + spec.yaml, and have the implementer only fill named TODO holes (storage decls + task bodies).
all_proposals.mechanism: New module code_translation/skeleton_ir.py. Phase 1 (deterministic): parse layout.csl with a small regex/AST pass (the same surface translation_facts.py already extracts — _IMPORT_FIELD_SCHEMAS table) plus spec.yaml to produce a CSL file with: (a) param block (verbatim from layout.csl @set_tile_code .{...}), (b) module imports with the correct field names (c2d_params, NUM_PES, sys_mod, timestamp, layout_mod) already filled in, (c) input/output queue reservations using IDs known to be free (memcpy reserves 0-1; halo gotcha says max-IQ on WSE-3 is 7 — pick from {2..7}), (d) local_task_id stubs starting from 12 (memcpy reserves 0-11), (e) empty fn f_xxx() void {} stubs that match the launch contract's @export_name list, with the canonical f_tic/f_toc bodies already inlined and frozen. The LLM is invoked ONLY on labelled // TODO(fill: storage), // TODO(fill: SEND_TASK_BODY), // TODO(fill: COMPUTE_BODY) holes — each prompted independently with just the local context. Wire into cuda2csl.py CUDA2CSLOrchestrator.translate() as a new code path gated by --skeleton-ir. The implementer prompt q_translate_cuda_to_csl_bundle becomes a per-hole prompt (q_fill_hole) seeded with the hole's name, the surrounding scaffold, and the CUDA fragment that maps to it (from the analyzer's section-by-section output).
all_proposals.why_now: Halo_recv_unblock cluster fails 6/7 because the implementer keeps mis-binding the halo state machine — wrong task IDs, wrong queue IDs, missing @unblock, hand-written unblock_cmd_stream, fabricated builtins on fn boundaries. dsr_queue_fabric_init (2/3 fail) is structurally identical: queue/DSR collisions at file scope. Both failure modes are at the SCAFFOLD level (param/import/queue/task plumbing), not at the algorithm level. If the scaffold is deterministically correct, the LLM cannot collide queue IDs or invent builtins because it never writes that code. This is structurally distinct from translation_facts (which told the LLM the rules and hoped it would apply them) — here the rules are enforced by code generation, not by prompt context.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Engineering: 3-5 days. Day 1: skeleton emitter from layout.csl + import schema. Day 2: hole template catalog (halo state machine, collectives_2d allreduce, single-PE pure-compute, host-driven RPC loop) — ~6 canonical halo holes. Day 3: per-hole prompt + wire into translate(). Day 4-5: A/B against hybrid_sweep on the 9-kernel failure corpus. Wall time: comparable to current pipeline (skeleton is deterministic + fast; per-hole LLM calls parallelize, ~3-6 calls per kernel of ~1k tokens each = cheaper than today's single 8k-token shot). LLM cost: similar or lower because each hole prompt has narrow context vs today's full layout+contract+CUDA+knowledge.
all_proposals.risk: Same shape as translation_facts ONLY if the holes don't compose into a working file — i.e. if the scaffold is rigid enough to be wrong for unusual topologies (e.g. Cholesky's launch.csl shape, or Mandelbrot's single-PE no-fabric case). Mitigation: start with halo cluster only (7 kernels, all 4-cardinal-neighbor topology) where the scaffold is highly stereotyped. If skeleton hole-filling produces 4+ passes on the 6 currently-failing halo kernels, the structural-vs-prompt argument is validated and we extend to dsr_queue cluster. The harder risk: the LLM might need to add hole declarations the skeleton omitted (e.g. extra storage); allow a final 'free edit' pass with a diff-size cap (≤30 lines) to absorb this without going back to free-text generation.

all_proposals.name: Executable mini-IR: Python reference runner that validates translation semantics pre-cslc
all_proposals.one_line: Build a tiny Python interpreter for a typed IR that captures CUDA kernel intent (grid/block, reads, writes, reductions, halo exchanges) and run it on the same test inputs as the CUDA reference; the architect emits this IR, we execute it for ground-truth output, and the implementer's CSL must produce numerically equal output on the simulator — gating before any expensive cslc attempt.
all_proposals.mechanism: New module code_translation/exec_ir.py defining ~12 IR ops: LOAD_TILE, STORE_TILE, EXCHANGE_HALO(direction, width), REDUCE(axis, op), BROADCAST(axis), GEMM_LOCAL, STENCIL_5PT, AXPY, DOT, FMA_VEC, ACTIVATE_TASK, SYNC_BARRIER. Architect emits this as JSON (new prompt q_emit_exec_ir, replaces or supplements DESIGN.md). A Python evaluator runs it on the CUDA test inputs (we already have CUDA reference outputs from kernels/*/CUDA/commands.sh runs) — if the IR's output doesn't match CUDA reference within tolerance, the IR is wrong and we re-prompt the architect (cheap: no cslc). Only if IR passes do we send it to the implementer alongside the CUDA source. After CSL compiles + runs, we compare CSL output not just to CUDA but ALSO to the IR's output — a 3-way agreement check that pinpoints whether failure is IR-level (bad design), CSL-level (bad implementation), or numerical drift. Wire into cuda2csl.py between architect and implementer phases. Reuse benchmark_csl.py output-collection plumbing for the comparison.
all_proposals.why_now: Today's pipeline has NO semantic gate between architect and implementer — the architect's DESIGN.md can be silently wrong (wrong tile decomposition, wrong reduction axis, wrong halo width) and the implementer faithfully generates wrong CSL. For halo kernels, the failure mode is often 'halo width is 1 but design said 2' or 'reduction is along Y but design said X' — caught only at end-to-end numerical check after cslc + sim (~5-10 min per attempt). The exec-IR catches it in seconds. For BiCGSTAB-class iterative solvers (currently 0/4 W2 lift, also W1 fragile), this gives a numerical oracle the optimizer can use to reject non-equivalent transformations without running them on hardware. Structurally distinct from translation_facts: this is an EXECUTABLE oracle that the architect's design must pass, not extra prompt context.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Engineering: 5-8 days. Day 1-2: IR opcode definitions + Python evaluator for the 8 W1-failing kernels (Laplacian halo, Cholesky, BiCGSTAB, CG, PCG, Power, GEMM_C2D, Residual). Day 3: q_emit_exec_ir prompt + JSON schema. Day 4: architect-IR validation loop (parse + execute + diff vs CUDA output). Day 5: wire into orchestrator. Day 6-8: A/B sweep + iterate. LLM cost: +1 architect call per kernel on success (IR JSON is small, ~500 tokens), +1-3 architect re-prompts on IR failures. Wall time per attempt: +30s (Python evaluator on 8x8 grid is millisecond-scale; only the LLM round-trip dominates). Net pipeline cost neutral if it catches 1-in-4 bad designs before implementer.
all_proposals.risk: The IR could be too restrictive (can't express a kernel) OR too permissive (passes designs that still translate wrong — e.g. an IR that's correct but where the implementer mis-binds the task graph and produces a deadlock cslc can't detect at compile time). Mitigation: start with the 4 halo-stencil-shape kernels where the IR ops list is small and well-known; if the IR can express them and the eval matches CUDA, extend. The other risk: this is morally similar to MLIR-style multi-level — and Phase 1 of multi-level IR has decades of warnings about who maintains the IR. Mitigation: don't build a general IR; build only what 8 kernels need, deferring generality. If after 8 kernels the IR has >30 ops, abandon — that's evidence we've reinvented MLIR.

all_proposals.name: CUDA-side AST IR: tree-sitter parse + structural feature vector for retrieval and gating
all_proposals.one_line: Finish the half of translation_facts that Phase 1 deferred — parse the CUDA source with tree-sitter into a typed AST, extract a structured feature record (grid/block dims, sync primitives, shared-mem usage, reductions, atomics, kernel topology), and use it (a) as the retrieval key for example matching, (b) as a gate on which W1 cluster the kernel belongs to, (c) as a contract the IR-from-CUDA emits that the architect must respect.
all_proposals.mechanism: New module code_translation/cuda_ir.py using tree-sitter-cuda (or libclang-python). Parse kernel.cu → emit a CudaKernelFacts dataclass with: kernels=[KernelDecl(name, grid_dim_expr, block_dim_expr, shared_mem_bytes)], syncs=[__syncthreads count + position], reductions=[(op, scope)], atomics=[(op, addr_pattern)], memory_pattern=(coalesced|strided|gather|halo_5pt|halo_9pt), reduction_topology=(tree|warp|shared), host_loop_iters_param, kernel_call_graph. Wire into cuda2csl.py as a Phase 0 step before analyse_cuda. Three slots into the pipeline: (1) the cluster detector currently in csl_knowledge_base._detect_w1_clusters_for_kernel uses string-match on the CSL spec — replace with deterministic CUDA-side detection (halo_5pt → halo_recv_unblock cluster; multi-kernel reduction graph → dsr_queue cluster; explicit grid stride loop with broadcast → collectives_2d cluster). (2) replace TF-IDF query with structural feature vector (cosine over normalized CudaKernelFacts fields) to retrieve from cerebras-csl-skills the example with the same memory_pattern + reduction_topology — current TF-IDF over prose retrieves on token overlap, not structure. (3) the analyser's free-form prose gets augmented with this structured facts block; the architect's DESIGN.md is then verified against it (e.g. if CUDA has __syncthreads inside a reduction loop, DESIGN must include a barrier task per iter).
all_proposals.why_now: Phase 1's CSL-side translation_facts told the implementer what CSL expects but never closed the loop on what CUDA actually said. Cluster detection currently relies on kernel name + ad-hoc string match (csl_knowledge_base.py L711) which is brittle — Single-Tile-Matvec was wrongly clustered as halo and got bad gotchas (#42 in task list fixed this manually). A deterministic CUDA-side classifier is robust and free at inference time. Retrieval is currently TF-IDF over prose (csl_knowledge_base.py L1068-1216), which retrieves on 'allreduce' word overlap rather than 'this kernel does a per-row reduction along Y axis' — exactly the W1 failure mode where the wrong example is retrieved. Structurally distinct from translation_facts: this is a NEW SIGNAL (CUDA AST → cluster + retrieval key), not new prompt text. The signal feeds existing slots; it doesn't add a slot.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Engineering: 4-6 days. Day 1: tree-sitter-cuda integration + 20-field CudaKernelFacts extractor, tested on all 15 W1 kernels. Day 2: structural cluster detector + A/B against current cluster detection (regression test: all currently-correct cluster assignments must still hold). Day 3: feature-vector retrieval (sentence-transformers MiniLM over CudaKernelFacts → JSON → embed; or just hand-weighted cosine over the field dict). Day 4: wire into csl_knowledge_base._augment_query_for_w1_clusters + _detect_w1_clusters_for_kernel. Day 5-6: A/B sweep on 15 W1 corpus. LLM cost: zero added (purely deterministic). Wall time per kernel: +2s for parse + retrieval.
all_proposals.risk: Same shape as translation_facts if the extracted facts just become extra prompt text that the LLM ignores. CRITICAL mitigation: the facts must DRIVE A DECISION (which cluster, which examples to retrieve), not just be added to the prompt. If the only use is 'inject CudaKernelFacts as YAML into the implementer prompt', this is translation_facts redux and will fail the same A/B. The decision-driving use is the load-bearing piece. Secondary risk: tree-sitter-cuda may not parse some kernels cleanly (e.g. heavily templated code, CUB/thrust intrinsics). Mitigation: graceful fallback to current TF-IDF + string-match path; ship as additive signal, not replacement.

all_proposals.name: Local constraint solver: queue/task/color allocator the implementer plugs into
all_proposals.one_line: Stop letting the LLM allocate task IDs, queue IDs, colors, and DSR IDs by hand — extract layout.csl's already-used IDs, run a SAT-style allocator that produces a JSON map (TX_N_QUEUE=2, SEND_TID=12, ...) the implementer must reference by name in its CSL.
all_proposals.mechanism: New module code_translation/id_allocator.py. Parse layout.csl + commands_wse3.sh to find: (a) memcpy-reserved input queues [0,1], (b) local_task_ids already used by layout (parse @get_local_task_id calls + the layout's tile-code .{...} struct passed task IDs), (c) colors already bound to fabric routes (parse @set_color_config + @set_routing), (d) DSR IDs claimed in collectives_2d imports. Compute the free set per resource (queue IDs 2-7 on WSE-3 minus any layout-claimed; local_task_ids 12-63 minus claimed; etc.). For each kernel, build a static plan: 'this halo kernel needs 4 TX queues + 4 RX queues + 4 task IDs + 1 compute task + 1 exit task' from cluster detection. Allocate. Emit as a JSON-ish facts block (NEW slot {allocated_ids} in q_translate prompt) AND wire into a post-generation linter: parse the LLM's CSL with a small regex pass, extract all @get_input_queue / @get_local_task_id / @get_output_queue calls, and reject the CSL if any call uses an ID not in the allocator's plan — failed CSL goes back to the implementer with a structured diff ('you used @get_local_task_id(0), allocator says use 12-15; correct it').
all_proposals.why_now: Direct hit on halo_recv_unblock + dsr_queue_fabric_init failure clusters. The halo gotchas distilled in B1 (task #65) document this exact failure mode: 'max input queue on WSE-3 is 7', 'IDs 0-11 reserved for memcpy', 'don't @unblock(0) — that's memcpy's lane'. These are HARD CONSTRAINTS that should be enforced by code, not by prompt. Today the LLM reads the gotcha and STILL allocates queue 1 or task 8 (the cluster keeps failing 6/7 even with gotchas active). The structural fix is to take the choice away from the LLM and verify in code. Structurally distinct from translation_facts: this is a SOLVER + LINTER feedback loop — the LLM is told valid IDs AND its output is automatically rejected if it ignores them, which is constraint propagation, not prompt context.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Engineering: 2-4 days. Day 1: parser for layout.csl resource claims (mostly regex; ground_gotcha.py already parses similar structures). Day 2: allocator + per-cluster resource plan templates. Day 3: post-generation linter + repair-loop wiring (reuse current repair loop in cuda2csl.py:translate's bucket-routed repair). Day 4: A/B on 7 halo kernels. Cheap because it's deterministic. LLM cost: net negative — fewer repair iterations because the linter catches ID collisions before cslc spends 30s failing on them. Wall time: -1 min per failed attempt that gets caught locally vs cslc.
all_proposals.risk: Risk this is too rigid — some valid CSL might allocate queues differently than the planner expects (e.g. a kernel that uses 6 queues instead of 4). Mitigation: allocator emits a RANGE of valid IDs per resource type ('queues 2-7 are free, use any 4'), and the linter checks set membership not equality. The LLM picks within the free set. Secondary risk: shape of translation_facts if we only inject the allocated IDs into the prompt without enforcement — must include the linter + repair gate. If the linter never fires (LLM always picks within the free set when prompted), then it IS just translation_facts and we'd discard. The A/B signal is: does the linter fire >20% of attempts? If yes, the loop is doing work.

all_proposals.name: Per-section CSL synthesis with cslc gate on each section
all_proposals.one_line: Decompose pe.csl into 5 sections (imports+params, storage, comptime bindings, task bodies, entry fns) and generate them one at a time, compiling-checking each addition with cslc before moving on — leveraging ground_gotcha.py's existing minimal-harness infrastructure as a per-section validator.
all_proposals.mechanism: New orchestrator method synthesize_sectioned() in cuda2csl.py. Section order: (1) param decl + module imports + queue/task/color decls (compiles with empty fn stub bodies), (2) storage decls (var x: [...] = @zeros(...); ptr exports), (3) comptime { @export_symbol(...); @bind_*_task(...); @activate(...); }, (4) task body fns (SEND, RX_DONE, COMPUTE, EXIT — one at a time, each compiled against stubs for the others), (5) entry fn bodies (f_run, f_tic, f_toc). After each section, build a minimal-harness pe.csl using ground_gotcha.py's _HARNESS_SINGLE_PE or _HARNESS_SEND_RECV_2X1 (whichever matches cluster), substitute the cumulative CSL written so far, run cslc; if it fails, the LLM gets the cslc error and the previous-section-snapshot and re-generates just that section. The full pe.csl is only assembled after all sections pass their per-section cslc gate. Reuse ground_gotcha._singularity_gate for serialization. New prompt template q_synthesize_section(section_name, prior_sections, cuda_source, design_doc).
all_proposals.why_now: The 8-attempts-per-kernel budget today is spent on round-trips where the LLM fixes one issue in a 200-line file and breaks two others. Halo kernels need ~6 task bindings + ~8 queue reservations + storage + 4 task bodies + entry fns to all be consistent — generating all of it in one shot is the failure mode. Sectioned synthesis bounds the blast radius: a broken task body re-prompts on that body only, not the whole file. cslc is the only oracle that catches typed-AST errors (wrong field name, wrong arity, wrong queue ID) before sim run. ground_gotcha.py already proves cslc-as-validator works for ~10-20s per check. Structurally distinct from translation_facts: this is INCREMENTAL CONSTRUCTION with EXECUTION at each step, not extra context up front.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Engineering: 5-7 days. Day 1-2: section decomposer (split a reference pe.csl into the 5 sections programmatically; test round-trip). Day 3: per-section synthesis prompt + harness builder. Day 4: cslc gate + per-section repair loop (cap retries at 3 per section). Day 5: wire into translate() as --sectioned mode. Day 6-7: A/B sweep. Wall time per kernel: ~5x more cslc invocations (5 sections × ~15s each = 75s, vs current 1 × 15s) but FEWER LLM round-trips (each section is small and rarely needs >1-2 retries vs current 8-attempt full-file repair). Net wall time roughly similar. LLM cost: each section prompt is ~30% of full prompt (smaller knowledge_base slice; sectioned context). Total LLM tokens may go DOWN despite more calls because per-call context is narrower.
all_proposals.risk: Sections may have non-local dependencies that break per-section validation (e.g. task body needs a storage decl from section 2; comptime block needs a fn from section 4). Mitigation: cumulative compilation (section 4 compiles all of 1+2+3+4, not just 4 in isolation) — already in the design. Real risk: latency. If 75s × 8 attempts × 9 kernels = 90 min/sweep this slows iteration. Mitigation: parallelize sections that don't depend (sections 2 and 3 can both compile against section 1; sections 4 and 5 in parallel against 1+2+3). Same-shape-as-translation_facts risk: NONE — this is fundamentally different (execution-gated incremental construction vs prompt context). If it fails, it fails for its own reasons (section decomposition is wrong, or per-section LLM prompts are still too underspecified), not the translation_facts failure mode.

all_proposals.name: Reference-CSL retrieval via structural similarity over ground-truth pe.csl corpus
all_proposals.one_line: Build a sentence-transformers index over the 30 working pe.csl files in csl-examples (with the W1 invariant respected — the index is consulted by the orchestrator, not shown to the implementer raw) and retrieve top-3 structurally-similar working pe.csl files, then extract just the patterns that match (task-graph skeleton, halo-exchange idiom) and inject those PATTERNS into the implementer prompt — keyed by CUDA-side AST features from proposal 3.
all_proposals.mechanism: New module code_translation/csl_corpus_retriever.py. Index build (offline, once): glob /home/USER/csl-examples/benchmarks/*/src/*.csl + kernels/*/CSL/pe.csl (the working ones — guarded by test_no_compute_leak.py to ensure no leakage into prompts). Embed each file with sentence-transformers MiniLM into a vector + extract structural facts (task count, halo direction set, collective_2d import yes/no, comptime block count). At inference time, take the CudaKernelFacts from proposal 3 + the cluster detection, query for top-3 closest pe.csl files. Then INSTEAD of injecting raw pe.csl (would violate W1 invariant), extract just the pattern templates: (a) task-graph skeleton (anonymized task names + bind/activate pattern), (b) halo-exchange idiom (anonymized: 'for direction in {N,S,E,W}: stage column → @fmovs async with .activate=RX_DONE_TID, decrement counter on RX_DONE, fire COMPUTE when counter==expected'). Inject these PATTERN abstractions into q_translate_cuda_to_csl_bundle as a new slot {worked_patterns}. Critically: the patterns are anonymized templates — symbol names, dims, and concrete IDs are scrubbed — so they teach STRUCTURE not specific code.
all_proposals.why_now: Today's RAG (csl_knowledge_base.py L1068 tutorial_context, L1216 skills_context) retrieves by TF-IDF over prose chunks of SKILL-*.md and tutorial READMEs — it surfaces WHAT-IT-SAYS, not WHAT-CODE-WORKS. The actual working pe.csl files in csl-examples encode the halo state machine, the collectives_2d call pattern, the DSR layout — far more concretely than any prose explanation. The compute-leak canary already exists (cuda2csl._set_compute_canary) and would catch raw pe.csl bleeding into the prompt. The mitigation is the anonymized-pattern extraction step. Structurally similar to translation_facts ONLY if the retrieved patterns are just dumped as text and ignored — to differentiate, the patterns must be small (<300 tokens each), structural (not prose), and cluster-keyed (only the matching cluster's patterns surface).
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Engineering: 3-5 days. Day 1: corpus glob + leak-guard (extend test_no_compute_leak to cover the retriever's output). Day 2: embedding index (MiniLM is ~80MB, single-machine; 30 files = trivial). Day 3: pattern-anonymization pass (regex scrub symbol names; convert dims to N×M placeholders; convert IDs to slot tokens). Day 4: wire into prompt_cuda2csl.q_translate. Day 5: A/B. LLM cost: +200-500 tokens per implementer call. Wall time per kernel: +1s for retrieval.
all_proposals.risk: HIGHEST risk of being same-shape-as-translation_facts in this list. Mitigation rule: only ship if anonymized patterns are STRUCTURALLY different from prose (i.e. they encode dataflow shapes, not lists of rules). Validation: before sweeping, hand-inspect 5 retrieved patterns and ask 'is this information already in csl_knowledge_base?'. If yes for >2/5, the corpus retriever is redundant — kill the proposal. Secondary risk: the W1 leak canary trips on the anonymized output, in which case the leak-detection is too aggressive OR the anonymization is too weak; need to harden _set_compute_canary's signal detection to look at NAMES not STRUCTURE. Tertiary: 30 pe.csl files is a small corpus; embedding-similarity may degenerate to 'always return the same 3 examples'. Mitigation: add cluster-bucket-filter before similarity ranking (only retrieve from the halo bucket if the query is halo).

all_proposals.name: Nearest-neighbor skeleton seeding from passing kernels
all_proposals.one_line: Before the implementer runs, retrieve the most structurally-similar PASSING pe.csl from our own kernels/*/CSL/, abstract it into a hole-punched skeleton keyed to the target's layout.csl, and feed it as a starting scaffold (not a worked example to imitate).
all_proposals.mechanism: Build an offline index of all currently-passing kernels/*/CSL/pe*.csl. The key for each entry is derived from its layout.csl signature: (rectangle_w, rectangle_h, declared colors, declared host-RPC symbols, # of fabric tasks, sender/receiver topology). At translation time, hash the target's layout.csl into the same key-space, pick the top-1 neighbor by signature distance (not text similarity), then run a deterministic abstractor that strips identifiers/sizes/numeric literals and replaces the function bodies of compute-loops with `// TODO: implement` markers — but KEEPS the task-graph wiring, DSD declarations, queue-id assignments, and microthread-id assignments verbatim. The result is a skeleton pe.csl injected as a starting state in cuda2csl.py's implementer step (new slot `{skeleton_seed}` in prompt_cuda2csl.py), with explicit instructions: 'replace TODO bodies, do not touch wiring'. The wiring (queues, microthreads, color/fabric_color routing) is the exact failure surface of the halo_recv_unblock and dsr_queue_fabric_init clusters — these are syntactic conventions that don't get re-derived correctly from prose.
all_proposals.why_now: halo_recv_unblock (6/7 fail) and dsr_queue_fabric_init (2/3 fail) are clusters where the agent rebuilds the same boilerplate from scratch every attempt. We HAVE working pe.csl files for Laplacian2D-Halo, 7pt-Stencil-spmv, Residual, GEMV — all use the same halo wiring patterns. The reason r4 canonical hints failed (per memory: 'too composed to fit in minimal harnesses') is that prose abstraction LOSES the wiring; this proposal does the opposite — keep the wiring, hole out the math.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 2-3 days. Offline index build: minutes (deterministic AST/regex pass over ~25 pe.csl files, no LLM). Per-attempt cost: zero extra LLM calls — the skeleton goes into the existing implementer prompt slot (~1-3KB of additional context, replacing some of the ~4KB tutorial_context block). Wall time: +0s. Total LLM marginal cost: ~0.
all_proposals.risk: STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from translation_facts/semantic_bridge: those were free-floating descriptive text the agent could ignore. A skeleton is a constraint surface — the implementer literally starts from it, so injection compliance is forced. Risk: leak (we serve our own ground-truth pe.csl with bodies stripped). Mitigation: reuse knowledge_persistence.bundle_identifier_set() + tutorial_leak_check() — already validated for skills_context. Second risk: bad-neighbor seeding (wrong skeleton chosen). Mitigation: signature-based, not text-based — distance over typed features is interpretable; we can require ≥3 of {colors, queues, microthreads, rectangle-shape} to match before injecting, else fall back to current behavior.

all_proposals.name: Compile-validated few-shot construction
all_proposals.one_line: Replace the static tutorial_context() chunks with a small bank of 8-15 minimal cslc-compiling 'idiom cards' that each demonstrate ONE wiring pattern (halo-recv, DSR queue init, collective barrier), and pick 2-3 cards per attempt based on the W1 cluster classifier.
all_proposals.mechanism: Hand-author (or extract via the existing ground_gotcha.py harness) one minimal compiling .csl per idiom: e.g. `halo_recv_unblock_4color.csl` showing a 4-color east/west/north/south halo with queue ids 2/3/4/5 and matching task unblock pattern. Each card is <60 lines, cslc-verified to compile to an ELF on wse3. Store as code_translation/idiom_cards/*.csl + a YAML index keyed by cluster and pattern. At translation time, cuda2csl.py's _augment_query_for_w1_clusters() already detects the cluster; extend it to also return a list of card filenames. Inject the FULL CARD VERBATIM (not a summary, not a chunk) into the implementer prompt under '## Verified compiling idioms for THIS cluster'. Different from skills_context because (a) authored to be minimal — no kernel-specific math, just the wiring; (b) compile-validated continuously by a CI hook that runs cslc on each card; (c) cluster-gated injection (we already have the classifier).
all_proposals.why_now: The 11 cluster-gated W1 gotchas are PROSE — they describe a fix but don't show working code. The 'don't fabricate' lesson from r2/r3/r4 halo workflow is exactly this: LLMs rederive syntax wrongly. A verified minimal compiling card is the smallest object that can ground a syntax choice. This addresses halo_recv_unblock and dsr_queue_fabric_init directly because both clusters fail on the wiring boilerplate, not the algorithm.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 4-5 days to hand-author and cslc-verify the initial 8-card set (ground_gotcha.py already gives us the compile loop). Maintenance: a CI run of cslc on each card after each SDK bump. Per-attempt cost: cards are ~0.5-1KB each, so 3 cards displaces some tutorial_context budget — net token delta likely flat. No extra LLM calls.
all_proposals.risk: Closer to translation_facts in shape (extra prompt context). KEY DIFFERENCE: the cards are EXECUTABLE artifacts that have been compiled to verify correctness, and they are minimal — the agent can paste the wiring almost verbatim. Translation_facts was a YAML manifest of facts ABOUT the language; this is sample code that IS the language. Risk of contamination: cards must contain NO bench-specific identifiers — enforce by reusing tutorial_leak_check() at index-build time and rejecting any card that shares >3 tokens with any benchmarks/*/pe.csl. Second risk: cards become stale if SDK changes — CI gate mitigates.

all_proposals.name: Retrieval over our own version_trace.json (success ICL)
all_proposals.one_line: Index every PASSING (cuda_input, generated pe.csl, reviewer_notes) triple from past sweeps and, on a new translation, retrieve the top-1 'this CUDA looks like that CUDA' precedent and condition the implementer on the prior successful translation.
all_proposals.mechanism: version_trace data already exists under results/cuda2csl/* with per-attempt outcomes. Build a one-time indexer (tools/build_success_index.py) that walks all results/, filters to PASSING final-attempt CUDA→CSL pairs, and extracts a feature vector per record: {CUDA AST signature (loop nest depth, shared-mem usage, atomicCAS presence, blockDim/gridDim shape), target spec.yaml's mesh dimensions, host-RPC symbol set}. At translation time, _augment_query_for_w1_clusters() also calls retrieve_success_precedent(target_cuda, target_spec) which returns the top-1 match or None. If match found AND structural-similarity score >0.7, inject under '## A similar CUDA→CSL translation that PASSED' showing (a) the source CUDA (de-identified), (b) the generated pe.csl, (c) a one-line note 'this is your strongest precedent — adapt sizes/colors but reuse the architecture'. Critically: we're shipping the agent its OWN previous success, not a tutorial.
all_proposals.why_now: Best hybrid run hit 6/15. That means we have 6 fresh, ship-quality (cuda, csl) pairs that the framework HAS NEVER USED as in-context examples. The implementer currently re-derives architectures it has previously gotten right. For W2's iterative-solver stall (0% wins), the same idea applies: there are passing optimizer attempts on related solvers — surface them as precedent.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 3-4 days (indexer + retrieval + de-identifier + prompt slot). Wall time per attempt: negligible (in-memory index of ~50-200 records). Token cost: +2-4KB per implementer prompt when a precedent is found. No extra LLM calls. One-time backfill: parse existing results/ tree (~minutes).
all_proposals.risk: Highest contamination risk of the proposals — we're literally serving prior CSL code. MUST enforce (a) hard exclusion of the target kernel itself from its own index lookup (kernel-name and spec.yaml-hash blacklist), (b) tutorial_leak_check() against the target's reference pe.csl (which the agent must NOT see anyway — the leak check verifies this invariant), (c) de-identifier pass that strips kernel names from comments. Different shape from translation_facts because (i) it's executable code, not facts; (ii) it's gated by structural similarity, not always-on; (iii) it scales with our own success — more wins → more useful index.

all_proposals.name: Two-stage retrieval: cluster-classifier → dense-embedding rerank
all_proposals.one_line: Keep the existing TF-IDF as a coarse first stage, but add a sentence-transformers (BGE-small) embedding rerank over the top-30 TF-IDF candidates using a query built from typed features rather than raw CUDA prose.
all_proposals.mechanism: Today csl_knowledge_base.tutorial_context() uses CerebrasKnowledgeBase.prompt_context() with TF-IDF, top_k=3-4. Replace its single-stage scorer with two stages: (1) TF-IDF returns top-30 (cheap, current code path); (2) encode each chunk + a STRUCTURED QUERY ('target: 4-color halo, queue-id pattern, microthread-overlap=yes, mesh=NxN, host-RPC=launch+stop') with BGE-small (~30MB on disk, runs CPU in <100ms for 30 chunks); (3) rerank by cosine, take top-3. The structured query is constructed by extracting features from layout.csl + spec.yaml + cluster classifier output — NOT by feeding raw CUDA text to the embedder (which is the failure mode of naive embedding retrieval over heterogeneous corpora). Plug into csl_knowledge_base.py's tutorial_context/skills_context retrieval slot.
all_proposals.why_now: Audit of current tutorial_context() output (logged in results/ab_tutorials_*) shows the top-3 chunks are often the same generic gemv tutorial regardless of cluster — TF-IDF over kernel-prose is dominated by high-frequency terms. The halo and dsr clusters' fail modes are wiring-specific; the chunks that would help are buried at rank 10-20 in current retrieval. Reranking against a typed query elevates them.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 2 days. Disk: +30MB for BGE-small. Per-attempt wall time: +0.1-0.3s (CPU-only). One-time corpus encoding: ~30s. No extra LLM calls. Adds sentence-transformers dependency to requirements.txt — already permitted by environment.micromamba.yml pattern.
all_proposals.risk: MOST AT RISK of being translation_facts-shaped — same slot, same content, just better ranking. If TF-IDF rank-1 vs embedding-rank-1 are mostly the same chunks (likely if the corpus is uniform), zero lift. Mitigation: BEFORE shipping, do an offline rank-overlap audit on the 15 failed W1 prompts — if rank@3 overlap >70%, abandon. Second risk: domain mismatch (BGE trained on web text, not CSL). Mitigation: use STRUCTURED query (typed features), not raw code — embeddings of natural-language feature descriptions against natural-language chunk titles is in BGE's sweet spot.

all_proposals.name: Differential debugger: compile-error → grounded-snippet retrieval
all_proposals.one_line: When an attempt fails to compile, capture the specific cslc error message + offending source span, retrieve the minimal compiling snippet from idiom_cards/ or kernels/*/CSL/ that demonstrates the construct, and inject ONLY that snippet into the bucket-B repair prompt.
all_proposals.mechanism: Today's debugger_agent classifies into buckets A/B/C and lets the next attempt re-derive the fix from the same context. Add a pre-processor in debugger_agent.py: parse cslc stderr (already captured in benchmark_csl pipeline) for the specific error class — undefined_builtin, queue_id_conflict, color_routing_mismatch, dsd_shape_mismatch, microthread_unblock_required, etc. For each error class, maintain a hand-curated lookup table → idiom_card filename (uses Proposal #2's bank). The bucket-B/C repair prompt then includes ONLY that one card under '## Verified fix for THIS error class', plus the failing line span. Critically: we're not adding more context — we're SHRINKING context to a focused, executable correction. Sits between debugger_agent.py's classification step and the repair prompt assembly in cuda2csl.py.
all_proposals.why_now: 8-attempt budget bump didn't help (per memory: 0/14 from attempts 5-8) because each retry re-derives from the same context. The debugger correctly identifies the bucket but the REPAIRER doesn't get differential signal beyond 'try again, here's why'. Pairing error-class → minimal compiling fix is the constraint-propagation step that translation_facts lacked.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 3-4 days (error-class parser + lookup table + 8-12 idiom_cards from Proposal #2 reused). Maintenance: add new error→card mapping when novel failures appear. Per-attempt cost: NEGATIVE token delta (we remove the broad gotchas block and substitute one focused card). No extra LLM calls.
all_proposals.risk: STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from translation_facts in a key way: this is FAILURE-CONDITIONED — only fires when we have a concrete cslc error, and the injected snippet is targeted at exactly that error. translation_facts fired unconditionally. Risk: error-class taxonomy too coarse → wrong card pulled. Mitigation: start with the 6-8 most common error classes from existing results/ logs (high coverage, low ambiguity); expand only as needed. Second risk: relies on Proposal #2 shipping first (idiom_cards bank) — these are paired.

all_proposals.name: AST-diff guided patch retrieval (post-compile-success, pre-numeric-fail)
all_proposals.one_line: When an attempt compiles but numeric_check fails, do an AST-diff between the generated pe.csl and the structurally-nearest passing pe.csl, surface the divergence as a 'these two routing/queue choices differ — here's how the passing version did it' hint in the repair prompt.
all_proposals.mechanism: Numeric-fail attempts are a specific bucket (D, sometimes folded into C). Today the repair prompt just re-attempts. Add post-compile, pre-numeric-eval hook in cuda2csl.py: if compile succeeds but numeric_check returns 'wrong values', invoke ast_diff_against_neighbor(generated_pe, target_layout) → returns a diff report keyed to wiring elements (queue ids, color set, microthread ids, fabric_input/output_dsd shapes, task activate/unblock pairings). The diff is computed against the same nearest-neighbor selected by Proposal #1's signature index. Inject as 'CRITICAL DIVERGENCE FROM A KNOWN-WORKING NEIGHBOR' in the repair prompt. The diff is structural (counts and topology), not textual.
all_proposals.why_now: We have observed numeric-fail clusters where the generated CSL compiles, runs, returns garbage — usually a queue/color routing inversion or a missing unblock. The current repair loop has no signal for this beyond 'output wrong'. AST-diff against a passing neighbor is exactly the constraint-propagation step missing from the loop.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 4-5 days (lightweight CSL structural parser — can be regex-based for the wiring subset we care about, NOT a full CSL parser). Per-attempt cost: zero LLM, ~50ms diff. Reuses the same neighbor index as Proposal #1. Idiom_cards not required.
all_proposals.risk: DIFFERENT from translation_facts because this is BOTH failure-conditioned AND executable-grounded (diff is computed from real code, not authored prose). Real risk: if the nearest neighbor is the wrong neighbor for THIS kernel, the diff hint misdirects. Mitigation: require neighbor signature distance below a tight threshold (cosine ≥0.85 over typed features); else suppress the hint. Secondary risk: numeric-fail bucket is small in our data — value depends on volume. Mitigation: backfill against existing results/ to count bucket-D attempts before committing to build.

all_proposals.name: Layout-extracted contract enforcement before LLM call
all_proposals.one_line: Parse layout.csl into a typed contract object (exported names, struct-param fields, color/queue ids, frozen params) and reject LLM output mechanically with a localized diff before benchmarking, so the model sees a deterministic 'you violated X' instead of a 30s cslc round-trip.
all_proposals.mechanism: Add code_translation/layout_contract.py: regex+brace-walk parser over layout.csl (the same brace-walker as contract_check.extract_function_body) that emits a typed object: {exported_symbols: [(name, sig)], import_modules: [(path, struct_fields_consumed)], color_ids: {name: int}, task_ids: {name: (kind, int)}, struct_params_with_fields: {name: [field_names]}, host_params: [names]}. After the implementer emits CSL (extract_code_block in cuda2csl.py:1410), run a deterministic 'contract diff' pass: every name referenced by layout (e.g. stencilParams.fabin_dsd) must appear in the compute file; every @export_symbol in compute must satisfy a corresponding layout reference; every host_param must be `param X: T;` and not shadowed. On violation, skip the cslc benchmark and feed the typed diff as the next-turn fix prompt (bucket C without LLM-reviewer call). This is constraint propagation, not extra prompt context: the agent gets a binary verdict on a deterministic check, and the wrong cases never burn the ~30s cslc + run.py round-trip.
all_proposals.why_now: The current bucket-C path waits for cslc 'undeclared identifier' errors and then asks the reviewer to identify the missing symbol. The halo_recv_unblock and dsr_queue_fabric_init clusters are dominated by name/contract-mismatch failures (e.g. compute doesn't bind recv_color_iq that layout exposes, or invents a different field name). Catching them pre-compile turns a 30s round-trip into a sub-second one and frees attempt budget for the genuinely-hard semantic failures.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 2-3 days for parser + diff + wiring + ~12 unit tests against existing kernels/*/CSL/layout.csl. Wall time per check: <100ms (regex over ~200 lines). LLM cost: negative — replaces failed cslc compiles with deterministic feedback, saves ~30s and one reviewer call per caught violation. Risk: parser bugs falsely reject valid CSL — mitigate by running contract diff against all 28 reference compute files in kernels/*/CSL/pe.csl and requiring 0 false positives before enabling.
all_proposals.risk: Different shape than translation_facts: this is mechanical rejection with code, not prose injection. The risk is parser fragility — if the regex misses an idiom (nested generic struct params, comptime-conditional exports), it false-rejects correct code. Mitigated by seeding from the existing 28 reference layouts. Secondary risk: many halo failures are NOT contract violations but runtime deadlocks (PE-with-no-work never calls unblock_cmd_stream), so this addresses the C-bucket cluster more than the B-bucket one. That's fine — it's targeted.

all_proposals.name: cslc-in-the-loop with isolated per-function compile cells
all_proposals.one_line: Generate the compute file in dependency order (imports → task bindings → entrypoints → helpers), and after each block call cslc against a minimal harness derived from layout.csl with the rest stubbed; reject and re-emit a block locally before continuing.
all_proposals.mechanism: New file code_translation/incremental_synthesis.py. Reuse ground_gotcha.py's harness machinery (it already runs cslc on minimal pe.csl wrappers in _singularity_gate-coordinated tempdirs). Decompose the implementer pass into 4 stages: (1) imports + params, (2) comptime task-id/color bindings + @export_symbols, (3) each `task` body, (4) each `fn` body. After stage N emit-then-cslc against a harness built from the real layout.csl + stub-bodies for stages N+1..4 (return zeros, no fabric ops). If cslc reports a localized error in the just-emitted block, re-prompt the model with stderr_tail + the partial code and only that block to fix — never re-emit prior accepted blocks. The harness skeleton comes from ground_gotcha._HARNESS_SEND_RECV_2x1/mesh_2x2 plus a new layout-conditional harness that auto-picks based on layout.csl's @set_rectangle dims.
all_proposals.why_now: Current single-shot implementer means a syntax error in line 30 invalidates the entire 200-line file and burns a full 30s cslc + reviewer + repair cycle. The halo cluster's repeat failures (6/7) often have one or two local syntax/idiom errors in the recv block while the rest of the code is fine; this loses information because the next attempt rewrites everything. Incremental compile keeps the good parts and isolates the bad block. Different from translation_facts in shape: it's execution-in-the-loop (cslc is ground truth), not more prompt context.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 1-2 weeks (block decomposer, harness builder from layout.csl, per-block prompt template, integration into cuda2csl.translate). Wall-time per kernel: up to 4 cslc invocations per attempt instead of 1, so ~120s/attempt instead of ~30s — 4x slower per attempt. BUT we expect attempt count to drop 2-3x since errors are localized, so net wall-time may be neutral or worse on easy kernels, better on hard ones. LLM calls per attempt: ~4 small calls instead of 1 large — comparable token cost, slightly higher latency. Risk: cslc may not give useful errors when the rest of the file is stubbed (unused-symbol warnings, partial-init complaints).
all_proposals.risk: Worst case is shape-isomorphic to halo-gotcha r4 (cslc-grounded but canonical patterns too composed to fit minimal harnesses) — the stubbed cells may not exercise the same cross-cell constraints that fail in the full compile. Mitigated by always doing a final whole-file cslc pass; the per-block passes are advisory/pre-filter, not replacement. Real risk: some idioms (e.g. fabin_dsd referencing a microthread ID declared in another block) MUST be co-located to compile, and that wrecks the decomposition; need to keep tight blocks (e.g. all DSD/microthread setup as one block, not split).

all_proposals.name: Self-consistency vote with kernel-level execution oracle
all_proposals.one_line: Generate K=4 independent translations in parallel with high temperature; score each by (a) does it pass benchmark? (b) if multiple pass, do they agree on output buffers? (c) if none pass, vote on the most common @export_symbol set + task-binding shape and use that as the architect's seed for the next attempt.
all_proposals.mechanism: Modify cuda2csl.py's translate() loop to fan out K parallel implementer calls with same prompt + temperature=1.0 (currently single-shot, T=0). Each candidate runs through _benchmark_current_code in parallel via asyncio + threads — benchmark_csl already supports concurrent staging via _singularity_gate. Scoring: 1pt for pass, 0pt for fail; among failing candidates, extract structural signature (sorted @export_symbol names, task-id bindings, import module list) and pick the modal signature as the 'group consensus' shape. Feed that consensus signature to the next architect respin: 'these 4 attempts agreed on these exports/bindings; one of them tried X. Reconcile and re-architect.' Reuses the existing best-of-N infrastructure (task #21) but applies it to W1 translation, not W2 optimization, and adds the structural-consensus extraction.
all_proposals.why_now: Current bottleneck for W1 is failure clusters where the model gets one element right (say, the right collectives_2d import) but wrong on another (queue ids), and another sample gets the opposite right/wrong split. With K=1 we never see the union of partial correctness. With K=4 + structural voting, we get a free 'best fragments' merge signal even when no single sample passes. Cluster-relevance: halo_recv_unblock 6/7 failures have inter-sample variation in WHICH PE branch forgets unblock_cmd_stream — voting on which exports/bindings appear across samples can surface the canonical pattern.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 3-5 days (parallel fanout, signature extractor, consensus prompt template, attempt-budget accounting — K candidates count as 1 attempt or K?). Wall time per attempt: ~30s for cslc but K parallel benchmarks fit in same wall window if we have K SDK shim slots; LLM call latency dominated by slowest sample. LLM cost: 4x per attempt. Total: budget probably halves to 4 attempts at K=4 instead of 8 at K=1 — net ~2x token spend per kernel. Risk: requires N parallel SDK shim slots; ground_gotcha uses _singularity_gate to serialize, so we'd need to verify the shim can handle 4 concurrent compiles or stagger them.
all_proposals.risk: Self-consistency literature mostly addresses semantic ambiguity in NL→code; here the failures are mostly mechanical (wrong builtin, wrong queue id) where votes may just amplify the most common WRONG answer (e.g. all 4 samples make the same halo unblock mistake because it's the natural-language reading of the CUDA). Mitigated by gating consensus on pass-rate: only use voting signal when at least 1 candidate passes OR all 4 share the SAME structural skeleton (indicating consensus on the shape if not the bugs). Could collapse to translation_facts-shape (extra context that doesn't propagate) if structural signatures are too coarse to discriminate.

all_proposals.name: Reverse translation as automatic differentiator
all_proposals.one_line: After each failed implementer attempt, invoke csl2cuda.py on the candidate, diff the regenerated CUDA against the original CUDA, and feed the semantic diff (not the raw stderr) as the repair signal — turning a compile failure into a 'your translation said X about the algorithm; the original said Y' message.
all_proposals.mechanism: We already have code_translation/csl2cuda.py (708 lines, fully working reverse translator). Add a new bucket-D path in cuda2csl.py's repair loop: when the candidate CSL parses but fails benchmark with status=compile_pass+runtime_wrong OR status=compile_fail+semantic-suspicious (heuristic: failure_reason mentions arithmetic, output, mismatch), invoke csl2cuda on the candidate to get back CUDA-back. Diff CUDA-original vs CUDA-back with a structural diff (function bodies, loop bounds, reductions — not text diff). Wrap differences as a prompt block 'your CSL implements algorithm X but the source CUDA was algorithm Y, specifically: [diff].' The reverse translation runs once per failed attempt and only on bucket-B repairs (not contract violations). Reuses csl2cuda existing infra; no new LLM provider needed.
all_proposals.why_now: Reviewer's bucket-B path currently dumps stderr + failure_reason at the implementer, but stderr is often opaque (a wavelet routing deadlock manifests as 'D2H read 0 bytes'). For semantic bugs in iterative solvers (CG/PCG/BiCGSTAB/Power-Method — all 0% W2 improvement, all show as runtime-pass-but-wrong-values), stderr is useless because there is no error. A CUDA→CUDA roundtrip diff would name the actual semantic gap (e.g. 'CUDA-back loops 1..N but original loops 0..N-1' or 'CUDA-back reduces with `+` but original uses fused-multiply-add'). Structurally different from semantic_bridge (which was prose mapping between primitives) because this is execution-grounded — the diff comes from a real reverse pass, not the model's beliefs.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 1 week (bucket-D classifier in reviewer; structural CUDA diff using clang AST or even a treesitter pass; integration into repair loop). Wall time per repair: +1 csl2cuda call ~20s + diff ~2s. LLM cost: +1 medium call per bucket-D repair, only fires when other signals are weak. Risk: csl2cuda has its own failure mode — if reverse translation itself produces garbage CUDA (because the CSL is malformed), the diff is meaningless. Mitigate by gating on csl2cuda producing parseable CUDA; otherwise fall through to bucket B.
all_proposals.risk: Same-shape-as-semantic_bridge risk: if the diff is presented as prose without a hard constraint to enforce, the implementer may just acknowledge it and re-emit the same wrong CSL. Differs because the diff is specific and grounded in real reverse-translator output (not generic primitive mapping). Real risk: most W1 failures are NOT semantic but contract/idiom (halo deadlock, missing unblock) — reverse translation won't help those. So this proposal addresses the W2 iterative-solver gap and a small slice of W1, not the dominant halo cluster. Position as targeted, not universal.

all_proposals.name: Iterative deepening: 1-PE prototype, then scale
all_proposals.one_line: For multi-PE kernels (halo_recv_unblock cluster, collectives_2d cluster), first translate to a 1-PE-only CSL bundle (with rectangle = 1x1, no fabric ops), get it passing, then ask the model to refactor for multi-PE — splitting the search into two smaller search problems with one passing checkpoint between them.
all_proposals.mechanism: Add a workflow flag --iterative-deepening to cuda2csl.py. When set + the kernel's spec.yaml has `requires_multi_pe: true` (new field), the orchestrator first synthesizes a 1-PE shim layout.csl (auto-derived: set_rectangle(1,1), drop all collectives/fabric color decls, expose only memcpy params) and runs the existing translate loop against it. If the 1-PE version passes (status=pass), enter a second phase: prompt the model with the working 1-PE compute file + the ORIGINAL multi-PE layout.csl, asking to scale up — 'this compute logic is correct; refactor to communicate over fabric using the colors layout.csl exposes.' Two budgets: 4 attempts for 1-PE, 4 attempts for scale-up. Reuses translate() machinery + bucket routing for each phase. The 1-PE layout shim generator is the only new ~200 LOC.
all_proposals.why_now: halo_recv_unblock 6/7 + collectives_2d 2/4 failures are dominated by the multi-PE communication layer, not the compute. Forcing the agent to get compute right first decouples the two failure modes — currently the agent jointly searches over (algorithm correctness, halo communication, queue/color setup) and the search space is too big. Empirical evidence: single-tile-matvec works (compute-only, no fabric), but the moment we add the fabric layer everything breaks. This proposes to honor that separation in the search structure.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 1 week (1-PE shim generator from layout.csl, two-phase orchestrator wrapper, scale-up prompt template, spec.yaml flag). Wall: 2x attempt budget per kernel in the worst case (4 1-PE + 4 scale-up = 8 vs current 8), so wall-time neutral if each phase converges. LLM cost: +50% in worst case (the 1-PE phase is cheap context, the scale-up reuses much of the 1-PE thread). Risk: not all multi-PE kernels have a meaningful 1-PE reduction — Cholesky's panel decomposition is inherently 2D, no useful 1x1 form. So this is opt-in via spec.yaml, not universal.
all_proposals.risk: Could be isomorphic to translation_facts in shape if the 1-PE phase's 'working code' doesn't actually constrain the scale-up phase — the model might rewrite from scratch and ignore the 1-PE solution as context. Mitigated by hard structural constraint: scale-up prompt must DIFF against the 1-PE version and justify each change. Real risk: the scale-up is the hard part anyway, and giving the model a passing 1-PE doesn't make scale-up easier if the bottleneck is canonical-pattern recall (which is what halo gotcha r4 found). Empirically test on 2-3 halo kernels before committing to the full 7.

all_proposals.name: Plan-then-verify: architect emits a checkable structural spec before implementation
all_proposals.one_line: Reshape the architect role from free-form DESIGN.md prose into a typed structural spec (YAML: imports, exports, task-bindings, comptime guards, per-PE branch table) that's mechanically validated against layout.csl BEFORE the implementer is invoked — preventing the implementer from spending an attempt on an architecturally-impossible plan.
all_proposals.mechanism: Add q_architect_structured_plan template (replaces existing prose-only q_design_decompose for opted-in clusters). Output is a strict YAML schema: {imports: [{module, alias, struct_args}], exports: [{symbol, type}], task_bindings: [{task_id_var, handler_fn, fired_from}], pe_branches: [{guard_expr, behavior}], fabric_ops: [{role: send|recv, color, queue_id, async, ut_id}]}. After emit, validate: every export must satisfy a layout.csl reference (reuses proposal #1's layout parser); every task_id_var must exist in layout; every fabric color must be declared in layout. On validation failure, REJECT the plan and re-prompt the architect with the typed diff — never let an unverified plan reach the implementer. The implementer's prompt then includes both the prose DESIGN and the validated structural spec; the spec is the contract, the prose is the rationale.
all_proposals.why_now: Current architect respins (bucket A) re-emit prose; the implementer then re-derives the structure and often gets a DIFFERENT structure than the architect intended, breaking the cycle. A structural spec gives both reviewer (when classifying B vs C) and implementer (when emitting) a single source of truth. Differs from translation_facts in shape: translation_facts was extra context appended to every prompt with no validation; this is a per-attempt validated artifact that fails-fast before the expensive step.
all_proposals.cost_estimate: Eng: 1-2 weeks (YAML schema, structural validator over layout.csl — shares parser with proposal #1, prompt templates for architect + reviewer + implementer that consume the spec, A/B replay harness similar to tools/ab_translation_facts.py). Wall time: +1 small architect call per attempt (validation is local), but eliminates ~30% of failed implementer attempts (estimated from manual classification of last 3 hybrid sweeps). LLM cost: marginal — architect is one of the smallest calls and already runs. Risk: schema gets ahead of the language — CSL has comptime constructs the schema can't express (recursive layout loops, conditional struct fields) and the architect must escape-hatch into prose; once that happens the validation degrades.
all_proposals.risk: Highest collision risk with translation_facts of all six proposals — it's an IR layer at the architect stage instead of post-extraction. The discriminator vs translation_facts: this IR is (a) validated against real layout.csl, not derived from regex; (b) authored by the LLM so it adapts to the kernel, not a fixed surface; (c) blocks downstream when invalid, not just decorates. If validation always passes (because LLMs are too good at making syntactically-correct YAML that's semantically wrong), it degrades to translation_facts shape and should be killed. Gate on: 'does the validator reject ≥1 plan per kernel on average on the failing-15 corpus?' If not, kill.

all_proposals.name: Compile-and-edit inner loop (cslc-in-the-loop drafter)
